title: Beginner Pack 4
subtitle: Everyday Actions — Destination, Direct Object & Polite Verbs
label: 3 patterns · 6 questions
rationale: Moves learners from static existence and identification (Packs 1–3) to active sentences using Level 1’s three action verbs (入る, 上げる, 下げる): (1) destination に extends Pack 1’s location に to mark the place someone enters with 入ります, (2) direct-object を extends Pack 2’s を下さい to mark what someone lifts (上げます) or lowers (下げます), and (3) polite present ます / ません lets learners state whether an action happens or does not happen.
description: Use Level 1 action verbs (入る, 上げる, 下げる) with destination に, direct-object を, and polite present ます / ません.

patterns.gloss: enter A / go into A (destination に)
patterns.readingNote: With motion verbs like 入ります (はいります, “to enter”), に marks the place you enter.
patterns.summary: In Pack 1, に marked where something stays (へやにあります). With movement verbs like 入る → 入ります (“to enter”), に marks the destination or space someone enters (へやに入ります).

examples.japanese: 大人がビルに入ります。
examples.reading: おとなが ビルに はいります。
examples.gloss: 大人 adult · ビル building · に into (destination) · 入ります enter

examples.japanese: あの人は駅に入ります。
examples.reading: あの ひとは えきに はいります。
examples.gloss: あの人 that person · 駅 station · に into (destination) · 入ります enter

questions.prompt: Choose the particle that marks ビル (building) as the place the adult enters:
questions.reading: おとなが ビル（　）はいります。
questions.gloss: 大人 adult · ビル building · 入ります enter

choices.explanation: Not quite. の connects two nouns (A の B), so it cannot link the destination noun ビル to the verb 入ります.
That’s right! With 入ります (“enter”), に marks the destination or enclosed place being entered (ビルに入ります).
Not quite. と means “and / with,” not the destination of 入ります (“enter the building”).

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Choose the particle that marks へや (room) as the place the two people enter:
followUp.reading: ふたりが へや（　）はいります。
followUp.gloss: 二人 two people · へや room · 入ります enter

choices.explanation: That’s right! に marks へや (“the room”) as the destination that the two people enter (へやに入ります).
Not quite. の links a noun to another noun, not to the action verb 入ります.
Not quite. か goes at the end of a sentence to ask a question, not between a place and 入ります.

workedExample.japanese: 二人がへやに入ります。
workedExample.reading: ふたりが へやに はいります。
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: Name the place being entered: へや (“room”). Step 2: Mark that destination with に (へやに). Step 3: Finish with the movement verb 入ります (“enter”).

questions.japanese: 女の人はホテルに入ります。
questions.reading: おんなの ひとは ホテルに はいります。
questions.gloss: 女の人 woman · ホテル hotel · 入ります enter

choices.text: There is a hotel entrance here.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 入り口 means “entrance” and あります means “there is,” whereas 入ります (はいります) is the action verb “enters.”
Not quite. “Lifts” is 上げます (あげます); 入ります (はいります) means “enters.”
That’s right! 女の人は sets “the woman” as the topic, ホテルに marks the hotel as her destination, and 入ります means “enters.”

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this new sentence mean?
followUp.reading: さんにんが えきに はいります。
followUp.gloss: 三人 three people · 駅 station · 入ります enter

choices.text: There are three stations at the entrance.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 三人 (さんにん) means “three people,” and 駅に入ります means “enter the station.”
That’s right! 三人が is “three people,” 駅に marks the station as the destination, and 入ります means “enter.”
Not quite. “Please give me” is を下さい, whereas に + 入ります means “enter.”

workedExample.reading: さんにんが えきに はいります。
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: 三人が = “three people” (actor). Step 2: 駅に = “into the station” (destination + に). Step 3: 入ります = “enter.”

patterns.gloss: do B to A (direct object を)
patterns.readingNote: The particle を is pronounced “o” and marks the thing directly acted upon by a transitive verb.
patterns.summary: Place を after a noun (A) to mark it as the direct object of an action verb (B), such as Level 1’s 上げる → 上げます (“to lift / raise something”) and 下げる → 下げます (“to lower something”).

examples.japanese: 大人が大きい箱を上げます。
examples.reading: おとなが おおきい はこを あげます。
examples.gloss: 大人 adult · 大きい箱 big box · を object marker · 上げます lifts
examples.english: The adult lifts the big box.

examples.japanese: あの人はかばんを下げます。
examples.reading: あの ひとは かばんを さげます。
examples.gloss: あの人 that person · かばん bag · を object marker · 下げます lowers

questions.prompt: Choose the particle that marks 大きい箱 (the big box) as the object being lifted:
questions.japanese: 大人が大きい箱（　）上げます。
questions.targetMeaning: The adult lifts the big box.
questions.reading: おとなが おおきい はこ（　）あげます。
questions.gloss: 大人 adult · 大きい箱 big box · 上げます lifts / raises

choices.explanation: That’s right! を marks 大きい箱 (“the big box”) as the direct object that the adult lifts (上げます).
Not quite. の connects two nouns (A の B), so it cannot link the object 大きい箱 to the verb 上げます.
Not quite. と means “and / with,” whereas 上げます needs a direct object marked by を.

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Choose the particle that marks かばん (the bag) as the object being lowered:
followUp.japanese: あの人はかばん（　）下げます。
followUp.reading: あの ひとは かばん（　）さげます。
followUp.gloss: あの人 that person · かばん bag · 下げます lowers

choices.explanation: Not quite. の modifies a following noun, not the action verb 下げます.
Not quite. に marks a location or destination, whereas かばん is the direct object being lowered.
That’s right! を marks かばん (“the bag”) as the direct object of 下げます (“lowers the bag”).

workedExample.japanese: あの人はかばんを下げます。
workedExample.reading: あの ひとは かばんを さげます。
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: Identify the thing being acted on: かばん (“bag”). Step 2: Mark it with the direct-object particle を (かばんを). Step 3: Add the transitive verb 下げます (“lowers”).

questions.japanese: 女の人は箱を二つ下げます。
questions.reading: おんなの ひとは はこを ふたつ さげます。
questions.gloss: 女の人 woman · 箱 box · 二つ two things · 下げます lowers

choices.explanation: Not quite. “Lifts” is 上げます (あげます, with 上), whereas 下げます (さげます, with 下) means “lowers.”
That’s right! 女の人は sets the topic, 箱を二つ marks “two boxes” as the direct object, and 下げます means “lowers.”

choices.text: There are two boxes under the woman.
choices.explanation: Not quite. “Under” is the noun 下 (した) with あります, whereas 箱を二つ下げます uses the transitive verb 下げる (“lowers two boxes”).

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this new sentence mean?
followUp.reading: ふたりが つくえを あげます。
followUp.gloss: 二人 two people · 机 desk · 上げます lift

choices.text: There are two desks in the room.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 二人 (ふたり) means “two people,” and 机を上げます means “lift the desk.”
That’s right! 二人が is “two people,” 机を marks the desk as the direct object, and 上げます means “lift.”
Not quite. “Lower” is 下げます (さげます), whereas 上げます (あげます) means “lift / raise.”

workedExample.reading: ふたりが つくえを あげます。
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: 二人が = “two people.” Step 2: 机を = “the desk” (direct object + を). Step 3: 上げます = “lift / raise.”

patterns.gloss: polite present positive vs. negative verb
patterns.readingNote: 〜ます states that an action happens (or will happen); 〜ません states that it does NOT happen.
patterns.summary: Polite action verbs end in 〜ます in the affirmative (入ります, 上げます, 下げます) and change 〜ます to 〜ません in the negative (入りません “does not enter,” 上げません “does not lift”).

examples.japanese: あの人はビルに入りません。
examples.reading: あの ひとは ビルに はいりません。
examples.gloss: あの人 that person · ビル building · 入りません does not enter
examples.english: That person does not enter the building.

examples.japanese: 一人では大きい机を上げません。
examples.reading: ひとりでは おおきい つくえを あげません。
examples.gloss: 一人で alone / by oneself · 大きい机 big desk · 上げません does not lift
examples.english: One does not lift a big desk alone.

questions.japanese: あの人はビルに入りません。
questions.reading: あの ひとは ビルに はいりません。
questions.gloss: あの人 that person · ビル building · 入りません does not enter

choices.text: That person does not enter the building.
choices.explanation: That’s right! ビルに marks the building, and 入りません is the polite negative of 入ります (“does not enter”).
Not quite. The affirmative “enters” is 入ります, whereas 〜ません in 入りません makes the verb negative (“does not enter”).

choices.text: There is no entrance in the building.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 入りません is the negative form of the verb 入る (“to enter”), not 入り口がありません (“there is no entrance”).

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this new sentence mean?
followUp.japanese: 女の人は箱を下げません。
followUp.reading: おんなの ひとは はこを さげません。
followUp.gloss: 女の人 woman · 箱 box · 下げません does not lower

choices.explanation: Not quite. “Lowers” is the affirmative 下げます, whereas 下げません ends in 〜ません (“does not lower”).

choices.text: Please give the woman a box.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 下げません is the polite negative of 下げる (“to lower something”), not 下さい (“please give me”).

choices.text: The woman does not lower the box.
choices.explanation: That’s right! 箱を marks the box as the direct object, and 下げません is the polite negative (“does not lower”).

workedExample.japanese: 女の人は箱を下げません。
workedExample.reading: おんなの ひとは はこを さげません。
workedExample.english: The woman does not lower the box.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: 下げます means “lowers.” Step 2: Changing 〜ます to 〜ません (下げません) makes it polite negative: “does not lower.”

questions.prompt: Choose the verb form that completes “That woman does NOT enter the river”:
questions.targetMeaning: That woman does not enter the river.
questions.reading: あの おんなの ひとは かわに（　）。
questions.gloss: あの女の人 that woman · 川 river

choices.explanation: Not quite. 入ります is the polite positive form (“enters”), whereas the target meaning is negative (“does NOT enter”).
Not quite. 上げます means “lifts / raises” (positive), not “does not enter.”
That’s right! 入りません replaces 〜ます with 〜ません to mean “does not enter” (“That woman does not enter the river”).

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Choose the verb form that completes “That person does NOT lift the big box”:
followUp.targetMeaning: That person does not lift the big box.
followUp.reading: あの ひとは おおきい はこを（　）。
followUp.gloss: あの人 that person · 大きい箱 big box

choices.explanation: That’s right! 上げません is the polite negative of 上げます (“does not lift”).
Not quite. 上げます is the positive form (“lifts”), whereas we need the negative “does not lift.”
Not quite. 入ります means “enters” (positive) and takes に, not 大きい箱を.

workedExample.japanese: あの人は大きい箱を上げません。
workedExample.reading: あの ひとは おおきい はこを あげません。
workedExample.english: That person does not lift the big box.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: 上げます means “lifts.” Step 2: Replace 〜ます with 〜ません → 上げません (“does not lift”).
